s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin and muscle symptoms following immunotherapy
salient_findings: Prominent erythema at nailfolds with dilated capillary loops
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Diagnosed with stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
Metastases in liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Received ipilimumab treatment
Developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab
Experienced initial improvement and later disease recurrence
Received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later
Symptoms recurred and worsened after second course of ipilimumab
Physical findings include diffuse erythema and edema
Elevated creatine kinase levels (1088 U/L and 1854 U/L)
Elevated aldolase levels (23.0 U/L)
Elevated C-reactive protein levels (28.6 mg/L)
Antinuclear antibody titer 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers

raw.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, and symptoms recurred and worsened after a second course of ipilimumab, suggesting a strong association between ipilimumab and the patient's myositis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory myopathy associated with cancer
rejected.why: While the patient has cancer, the temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and symptom onset suggests a more direct link to the medication rather than the cancer itself.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic myositis
rejected.why: Paraneoplastic syndromes are typically associated with the underlying cancer, but the patient's symptoms seem more closely related to the ipilimumab treatment.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and lab results are consistent with myositis, but the specific pattern of skin involvement and the temporal relationship with ipilimumab treatment make dermatomyositis a less likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
rejected.why: The muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers without evidence of inflammatory myositis or necrosis, making necrotizing autoimmune myopathy an unlikely diagnosis.
